speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) in the last three years, how many complaints has the Traffic Police received about noisy vehicles; (b) how many of these pertain to Nee Soon South; (c) whether there are adequate speed cameras installed in the areas; and (d) whether the Traffic Police will step up enforcement along Yishun Avenue 1 and Yishun Street 51, especially on Friday and Saturday nights.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: TP will continue to monitor the situation in Nee Soon South, and further adjust their operations as needed.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It seems like the Senior Parliamentary Secretary only mentioned closed-circuit television (CCTV) or speed cameras.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: A Swedish report published in 2009 found people who were regularly exposed to traffic noise in excess of 50 decibels were 40% more likely to suffer a heart attack than those who live in quieter neighbourhoods.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, my question: is there a cap on the upper limit of decibel or noise emitted by vehicles in Singapore?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Second, there are many other technologies used in other countries.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: For example, the United Kingdom uses automatic number plate recognition technique to dish out fines to drivers over excessive noise.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In Calgary, a Canadian city, is using sound camera and fining motorists with excessively loud vehicles.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And similarly, the Abu Dhabi police has invented noise-measuring cameras, which will help officers take action against abnormally loud cars, and also intelligent speed bumps flattened when you are driving slowly.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, is Singapore exploring some of these new technologies instead of just depending on speed cameras?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: They may not speed, but then it is very noisy and wake the residents up.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The last question is, will there be any action taken against workshops which illegally modify or do the modification to the motorcycles or the cars?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: New vehicles must meet the set noise admission standards before they can be registered for use in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, I have talked about speeding as well as the illegal modification of vehicle exhaust systems.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: TP and the Land Transport Authority (LTA) work together to address these issues.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: When there is feedback received, TP and LTA can conduct enforcement operations together.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On the Member's point about the new technologies, I will have to find out more from her.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: If the Member does not mind and surface those reports to me, and I will have my TP and LTA colleagues take a closer look at them.
